casual.plain_meaning: Everyday clothes you would wear to class. Clean and put-together, nothing torn or stained.
casual.formula: Jeans or casual trousers + tee, sweater, or casual shirt + sneakers or flats.
do: A good knit makes it look intentional
avoid: Gym wear unless it is a sports event
casual.designer_rule: Casual still has a silhouette. One fitted piece + one relaxed piece looks chosen, not thrown on.

smart casual.plain_meaning: One step up from class clothes. Relaxed, but you look like you thought about it.
smart casual.formula: Dark jeans or chinos + knit, polo, or button-down + loafers, clean leather sneakers, or ankle boots. A soft blazer is optional.
do: Swap the tee for a knit or shirt
Leather shoes or very clean minimal sneakers
smart casual.designer_rule: Upgrade one piece from your casual outfit, usually the shoes or the top. That is the whole trick.

business casual.plain_meaning: Office clothes without a full suit. No jeans, no sneakers. This is the default for most MBA recruiting events.
business casual.formula: Tailored trousers, chinos, or a midi skirt + blouse, button-down, or fine knit + loafers, flats, or low heels. A blazer is a plus but not required.
do: Trousers with a crease or a structured skirt
Collared shirt, blouse, or fine-gauge knit
avoid: Anything you would wear to a party
business casual.designer_rule: Look at the fabric, not just the item. Wool, cotton poplin, and fine knits read business. Jersey, denim, and fleece read weekend.

business professional.plain_meaning: The suit level. For interviews, superdays, client meetings, and formal presentations.
business professional.formula: Matching suit, or a blazer with tailored trousers/skirt in a dark neutral + crisp shirt or shell + polished closed-toe shoes.
do: Matching jacket and bottom when you have one
business professional.designer_rule: A suit is a uniform. Let one quiet detail (a good watch, a silk shell) be the personality.

cocktail.plain_meaning: Evening dressy. Galas, formal dinners, weddings that are not black tie.
cocktail.formula: Knee-to-midi dress or a sharp dark suit/jumpsuit + heels or dress shoes + one statement accessory.
cocktail.designer_rule: Evening is about texture and shine. A plain black dress becomes cocktail with one statement piece.

situations.name: Coffee chat with a company
situations.tip: Business casual. Dress like the company's office on a normal day. Bankers and consultants: lean toward a blazer. Tech and startups: a sharp knit is enough.

situations.name: Case interview / job interview
situations.tip: Business professional unless the recruiter clearly said otherwise. You will never lose points for being one step too formal at an interview.

situations.name: Recruiting info session / corporate presentation
situations.tip: Business casual. The firm's people will be there, so treat it like a short interview.

situations.name: Career fair / trek / office visit
situations.tip: Business casual for most firms. For banking or consulting treks, bring a blazer.

situations.name: Club mixer / networking happy hour
situations.tip: Smart casual. If it comes right after a recruiting event, just take off the blazer.

situations.name: Student presentation / class pitch
situations.tip: Business casual. You are on stage, so pick something that fits well standing up.

situations.name: Gala / formal dinner
situations.tip: Cocktail unless the invite says black tie.

situations.name: First date
situations.tip: Smart casual at effort 3: look like yourself on a great day. One polished piece, one relaxed piece, one focal point. Comfortable shoes you can walk in.

situations.name: Meeting a partner's parents
situations.tip: Smart casual at effort 4: neat, warm, and modest. Think 'favorite niece', not 'night out'. Soft colors and good fabric.

situations.name: Wedding guest
situations.tip: Cocktail unless the invite says otherwise. Never white or ivory. Garden or daytime weddings: lighter fabrics and block heels or flats.

situations.name: Dinner or drinks with friends
situations.tip: Smart casual, effortless. Jeans are fine — upgrade the top or the shoes.

situations.name: Brunch / weekend plans
situations.tip: Casual and comfortable with one nice detail — a good knit, a fun earring.

situations.name: Concert / party
situations.tip: Smart casual with more personality: one bold piece, shoes you can stand in all night.

effort_scale.1: barely tried — comfy, fine for errands
effort_scale.3: effortless — put-together, but it looks easy (the sweet spot for dates and friendly coffee)
effort_scale.4: polished — clearly dressed for the moment (interviews, meeting the parents)
effort_scale.5: dressed up — evening events, weddings, galas

effortless_rules: Mix one polished piece with one relaxed piece (blazer + tee, silk skirt + chunky knit).
Texture over shine: knit, linen, suede, washed silk read easy; sequins and stiff satin read like trying.
One focal point only — a color, a neckline, or a piece of jewelry, not all three.
Imperfect details: roll the sleeves, half-tuck the top, leave one button open.
Shoes set the level: a sneaker or flat brings any outfit down one notch, a heel brings it up one.
Fit beats formality: a piece that fits perfectly looks intentional without looking stiff.

fit_rules.shoulders: square neck, boat neck, off-shoulder, or sleeveless tops
fit_rules.waist: defined-waist pieces, high-waist bottoms, a tuck or a belt
fit_rules.legs: high-waist bottoms, straight or cropped trousers, shorter hems, pointed shoes
fit_rules.arms: sleeveless tops, or roll the sleeves
fit_rules.neck: V-necks and open collars, hair up
fit_rules.relaxed_areas: where someone prefers a relaxed fit, choose relaxed, flowy, wide-leg, or A-line pieces there — never clingy fabric there
